trust_decision.summary: Whether the 4-byte little-endian decompressed-length header may be used as an allocation size or as a write length is decided per overload inside LZ4DecompressorWithLength: it must be validated against the compressed size (at most 255 bytes of output per input byte), against a configurable allocation cap (64 MiB default), and against the caller's destination; the header parser and the low-level allocating decompressors are deliberately left permissive.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only the summary ('5-byte input triggers a 1 GiB allocation') lands here: the allocating convenience overload reads the header with getDecompressedLength and passes it straight to fastDecompressor.decompress(src, srcOff+4, destLen), whose implementation allocates new byte[destLen] (LZ4FastDecompressor.java:110).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The allocating primitives take the length as a caller contract parameter, not as parsed data, so guarding them looks like breaking the documented LZ4FastDecompressor/LZ4SafeDecompressor contracts (destLen/maxDestLen are 'the exact size of the original input'), and every in-library caller passes a validated value.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The non-allocating copy overloads must keep accepting declared lengths above the configured allocation maximum and must never apply that maximum to a caller-supplied destination: with maxDecompressedLength=15, decompress(compressed, 0, new byte[16], 0) must still succeed while decompress(compressed) throws (fix.diff:318-330, configuredMaximumOnlyLimitsAllocatedOutput); the constructor must also accept a limit of 0 (fix.diff:332-351). Existing round-trip tests already exercise the copy overloads with real payloads (src/test/net/jpountz/lz4/AbstractLZ4Test.java:151-296).

byte[] with explicit srcOff + srcLen on the safe-decompressor branch
ByteBuffer whose position is advanced by the call

declared length values: negative (high bit set), impossible for the compressed size (>255x), above the configured maximum, above the remaining destination

O7_producer.where: src/java/net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4CompressorWithLength.java:45-57 (putOriginalLength for byte[] and ByteBuffer, written by compress at :157 and :198)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The public static accessor getDecompressedLength(byte[] / byte[],int / ByteBuffer / ByteBuffer,int) still returns the raw header, so the documented way to size a destination for the copy overloads (new byte[getDecompressedLength(src)]) remains unbounded; the published fix only reworded its javadoc to 'without validating it against the compressed data'.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix itself documents this accessor as returning the length without validation, and the copy overloads legitimately need the raw declared value to compare against the destination, so validating/throwing in the parser looks like a caller-responsibility change.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and class as the landing point (a second public surface, not another package)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second WithLength-style wrapper (a frame, buffer or stream variant) that parses a declared length and delegates to this allocating primitive
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: LZ4DecompressorWithLength is itself just such a wrapper, and this primitive is the only way to get an allocated output in this library, so any new format helper a maintainer adds would reuse it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An LZ4UnsafeDecompressorWithLength-style generated twin under src/java-unsafe
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The build already generates Safe and Unsafe variants of every compressor and decompressor from templates, so mirroring the WithLength class in the other source root is the repository's own idiom.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pre-sizing rawBuffer from the frame's declared CONTENT_SIZE instead of the BD block maximum
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: expectedContentSize is already parsed from the untrusted header and left unused (only compared at :274), so sizing a buffer from it is the obvious optimisation and would recreate the same unvalidated-allocation defect.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A decompress(src, srcOff, srcLen, dest, destOff, maxDestLen) overload mirroring the safe decompressor
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The compressor twin already has exactly that maxDestLen overload (LZ4CompressorWithLength.java:155-159), so the asymmetric decompressor overload is a natural next addition.

O9_family: Uncontrolled memory allocation (CWE-789) from an unvalidated declared decompressed length; same methods also allow an out-of-bounds write into a too-small destination (CWE-787) and a negative length
